header:
Date: 2026-03-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Location: Zoom | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sam (Redwood CSM) + Alicia, Devon, Rina, Owen, Lukas (Newport Galley)
summary: Kickoff for Newport Galley's onboarding and pilot. Discussed goals (pilot success criteria, latency/cost targets), infra options (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC), security needs (SOC2, KMS, SAML), staging access plan and initial data/traffic requirements. Agreed on runbook delivery, security questionnaire timeline, and a staging walkthrough. Next: runbook and pilot criteria to be shared; staging access setup; security docs exchanged.
topics: Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick intro round, then we'll go into goals for the pilot and runway.
[00:18] Alicia (Customer): Hi all, Alicia here. We're excited to get Redwood in the loop — main objective is to replace our current ad-hoc LLM batch job with real-time inference for search and help center.
[00:30] Priya (SE): Nice, thanks Alicia. quick clarifying question, do you expect sub-200ms p95 on generation or is p50 more realistic for the pilot?
[00:45] Alicia: Ideally p95 < 400ms, p50 < 150ms; cost is also a factor. we want to show latency improvements vs their current setup.
[00:58] Devon (Infra): we run on GCP, mostly E2/combination, and we have a VPC peering setup for partners. we'll need VPC deployment or at least secure peering.
[01:15] Jordan: great, that maps to the Private option (VPC) or Dedicated depending on throughput. for the pilot we typically recommend hosted to start fast then move to dedicated if predictable throughput required.
[01:36] Rina (PM): timeline wise we're targeting a 6-week pilot, business wants decision by end of Q2.
[01:44] Sam (CSM): that's doable, our usual onboarding runway for pilot is 4–6 weeks with a staging access walkthrough week 1.
[02:00] Owen (Security): quick flag — we need to understand KMS options and audit logs. also SOC2 scope, encryption at rest and in-flight, and SSO.
[02:12] Priya: absolutely — Redwood supports BYOK via KMS/HSM integrations, plus audit logs and token-level tracing in the console. we'll share the security pack.
[02:25] Devon: when you say KMS, is that customer-managed key in their project or in Redwood? we prefer to have control.
[02:33] Priya: both supported: you can bring your own key for private deployment, or we can manage keys for hosted with rotation policies. we'll document the tradeoffs. apologies, sometimes our doc has 'Key-management' abbreviated odd, so we'll be explicit.
[02:52] Lukas (Eng): did you mention prefix caching or KV cache? how does caching play with fresh responses?
[03:02] Priya: good point, we have prefix and KV cache features that reduce cost for repeat prefixes — for QA traffic it's tricky because you need freshness, we can tune caching TTLs or disable for certain routes. sometimes transcripts show 'KV cash' in notes, sorry for the word swap — that's our bad transcribe.
[03:20] Jordan: to frame success: a pilot acceptance criteria doc — we want measurable goals: two sample flows, latency targets, cost per 1k tokens, and no regressions on our eval prompts. Alicia, can you confirm two canonical prompt sets?
[03:36] Alicia: yes, search rank rerank and help-center summarization. we'll send them.
[03:42] Rina: also an SLA question — we need to understand outage impact for our users. what does Redwood provide during pilot?
[03:50] Sam: for pilots we offer a best-effort SLA; if you move to Dedicated there's SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. we'll map the pilot to a playbook for fallbacks — e.g., degrade to shorter sequences or smaller model when capacity constrained.
[04:12] Owen: can you show the network flow for VPC peering and where logs land?
[04:20] Priya: yes, we'll include a simple infra diagram in the runbook — it shows request path, optional peering, and S3-like object storage for logs/audits.
[04:34] Devon: on peering, is egress charged by Redwood or us? we need cost clarity.
[04:40] Jordan: cost depends on deployment. for Dedicated/Private you largely control cloud egress; hosted includes egress in the usage bill sometimes. we'll include cost notes in the runbook spreadsheet.
[05:00] Rina: what about model versioning and rollbacks — we have compliance that requires ability to pin model versions.
[05:08] Priya: Redwood supports model pinning and can do canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. we'll detail the rollout steps and how to trigger a rollback.
[05:22] Alicia: OK. for the staging walkthrough, who should be present from your side — infra only or app devs too?
[05:30] Sam: infra + the primary integrator (Lukas) are ideal. then we'll expand to product stakeholders on the evaluation call.
[05:45] Devon: sample traffic — we can extract a 24-hour histogram and send. how granular?
[05:52] Priya: token-level histogram across time-of-day is ideal, and we'd like 95th percentile sequence length, percent of streaming calls, and typical concurrency. that lets us size Dedicated pools or recommend batching configurations.
[06:12] Lukas: small nit — our convos often have streaming chat and single-shot summarization. will Redwood support streaming responses + tool calling?
[06:22] Jordan: yes streaming and function/tool-call patterns are supported. we'll show examples in SDK.
[06:30] Rina: on security questionnaire, we use an internal vendor security form — can Redwood return answers in that format?
[06:37] Owen: and can you attach latest SOC2 and any penetration test summaries?
[06:40] Jordan: yes, we'll put SOC2 and the security pack in the shared drive. for pen test summaries we can discuss NDA gating if required.
[06:55] [08:00] Priya: (walkthrough) initial infra options: 1) Quick-hosted pilot (fastest), 2) Dedicated reserved pool (predictable throughput and isolation), 3) Private VPC deployment (full network control). each has tradeoffs on latency, cost, and time to provision.
[08:25] Devon: provisioning Dedicated — how long typically?
[08:29] Sam: usually 2–3 weeks after contract for capacity and infra; private VPC can be slightly longer depending on network approvals. Hosted is immediate.
[08:44] Rina: we're leaning hosted to start, but want the option to move to dedicated mid-pilot if performance shows. is that possible?
[08:52] Priya: yes; routing policies allow blue/green and fallback between hosted and dedicated. we can simulate costs for both in the spreadsheet.
[09:10] Lukas: any hard limits on concurrency per model in hosted?
[09:16] Priya: there are soft limits; we'll propose autoscaling policies and suggest burst options. we'll also show how to throttle token-level concurrency.
[09:30] Owen: about audit logs — retention policy? we need 1 year for specific events.
[09:36] Jordan: audit retention is configurable for enterprise, but for hosted there are retention tiers; we'll include options and pricing.
[09:50] Alicia: good, I want the runbook to be explicit about who does what on day 0 of pilot.
[09:56] Sam: absolutely — the runbook will have a day-by-day checklist and contact list.
[10:08] [15:00] (longer discussion on acceptance criteria, tradeoffs)
[15:12] Priya: technical checklist for staging: API keys, network allowlist, sample payload, model selection, and eval harness. we'll provide an example Postman and a small Python SDK snippet.
[15:30] Devon: does Redwood support private subnets only with no public egress? some of our data rules require zero public egress.
[15:38] Priya: yes for Private on-prem or VPC you can enforce private-only egress; we support S3-style endpoints and internal logging sinks. we'll capture exact requirements in the runbook.
[15:55] Rina: eval harness — will Redwood run A/B tests across models? we want side-by-side evaluation on the same prompt set.
[16:03] Priya: yes, the platform supports A/B and can capture quality metrics and regressions tied to prompt sets. we can hook into your existing eval dashboards via simple CSV exports or API.
[16:18] Jordan: one small commercial note — pilot pricing is usage-based but we also offer short-term reserved capacity if you want price certainty. we'll include both scenarios.
[16:30] Alicia: that helps. also need a POC success meeting scheduled at the end of week 4.
[16:37] Sam: we'll schedule that; goal is to review metrics, spikes, cost, and recommend next steps.
[16:45] Owen: can we get an SLA for the pilot? even if informal.
[16:49] Jordan: we'll put a pilot SLO in writing in the runbook. for production we move to formal SLA.
[17:00] [25:00] (discussion on sample datasets, redaction, and PII)
[25:10] Owen: redaction and PII controls are critical. we need to know what logs are captured and whether request/response can be redacted before storage.
[25:20] Priya: we support server-side redaction and configurable logging policies. you can disable response logging for certain routes; for more advanced PII redaction we can integrate with your DLP tool or provide a pre-processing hook.
[25:42] Devon: what's the process for rotating keys and decommissioning staging once pilot ends?
[25:49] Sam: we'll document key rotation cadence and decommission steps in the runbook. keys can be revoked and we recommend rotation monthly for pilots where customer-managed KMS is used.
[26:10] Rina: integration points — we want SDKs for Go and Python.
[26:18] Priya: current SDKs are Python, Node, and Go experimental. we'll share code snippets and a quickstart repo link. please note the repo name sometimes gets transcribed oddly — it's 'redwood-infer' but transcripts may show 'redwood infern' occasionally.
[26:35] Lukas: any restrictions on model artifacts we can bring in? we have some internal fine-tuned checkpoints.
[26:43] Priya: for Private you can bring your own model artifacts; for hosted we have a model catalog and can host customer models with contract terms. we'll provide guidance on size limits and supported formats.
[27:00] [35:00] (planning staging walkthrough and sequencing)
[35:10] Jordan: action recap — Jordan will send runbook and pilot criteria, Priya sets up staging creds and infra diagram, Owen returns security answers, Alicia sends prompt sets and traffic histogram.
[35:28] Priya: scheduling — how about staging walkthrough Tuesday 2026-03-31 16:00 UTC?
[35:34] Devon: that works for us.
[35:38] Rina: timezone note, some of our PMs are in PST, please avoid late evenings.
[35:44] Sam: noted, we'll pick reasonable times.
[35:50] Jordan: any other open questions?
[35:54] Devon: just one: can we advertise the pilot as private? we want to make sure the business isn't blocked by language that says 'hosted' in contract.
[36:02] Jordan: we'll make sure pilot paperwork clarifies deployment options; default is hosted pilot unless you select private and sign off.
[36:15] Owen: last thing, are there known gotchas with streaming + kvcache on low-latency paths?
[36:22] Priya: streaming and KV cache interact in nuanced ways. for low-latency streaming it's best to minimize background batching and set small batch windows; KV cache is beneficial for repeated prefixes but can add tail latency if not tuned. we'll include tuning knobs.
[36:40] Alicia: thanks, this is helpful. excited to see the runbook.
[36:45] Jordan: we'll follow up with all artifacts. thanks everyone.
[36:50] [End of recorded highlights — final 15 minutes included Q&A, sequencing of pilot days 0-30, and scheduling notes.]
